Elena —

Appreciate the clear asks. We can provide a concise mapping and evidence package before EOD Aug 11. High-level plan:

- Day 1 (today): Send NIST RMF mapping PDF and EU AI Act positioning memo (attached).
- Day 2 (Aug 11 morning): Share sample evaluation report for BRH-like slices, the evaluation harness description, and a short playbook for regression detection and alerts.
- Deliverables will include: Redwood_NIST_Mapping_20260811.pdf, Redwood_EU_AIAct_Positioning_20260811.docx, sample-eval-report-BRH-slice-202607.pdf, and a link to a shared Drive folder with logs samples and the SOC 2 extract (redacted).

Quick points up-front:
- NIST mapping: we map our controls and processes to NIST AI RMF subcategories; we link automated monitoring (behavioral metrics, distributional drift), access controls (IAM + KMS), and incident response runbooks for model failures.
- EU AI Act: our hosted API is treated as a provider offering a tool that may be deployed by BRH; classification depends on BRH’s usage (clinical decision-support examples can be high-risk). We document mandatory measures (risk assessment, documentation, human oversight guidance, logging and traceability). For customers in-scope we offer additional contractual controls and telemetry retention options to meet Article 28/29 expectations.
- Eval/regression: we run deterministic evals on pre-registered prompt sets + held-out clinical slices, maintain an anchored baseline model per customer, and trigger automatic regression flags on metric delta thresholds (e.g., answer-level accuracy, hallucination rate, safety classifier score).

I’m looping Monica (solutions engineering) and Markus (product security) to add technical and compliance detail. If you prefer a working call, propose 11:00–12:00 PT tomorrow.

Best,

Hi Elena —

Following Rohan’s note, I’ve summarized our evaluation and regression management approach below (this will be in the sample eval report and the Drive folder):

Evaluation harness (short):
- Test orchestration: Pytest-based harness with reproducible seeds, model version pinning, and dataset manifests (CSV + metadata JSON).
- Data slices: clinical domain slices (specialty, note type), demographic parity checks, OOD tests, safety-sensitive prompts. Each slice stores provenance and sampling metadata.
- Baselines and anchors: we keep a customer-anchored baseline snapshot. New model variants are benchmarked against the baseline using paired A/B evals and statistical tests (paired bootstrap for F1/accuracy, McNemar for categorical).
- Metrics tracked: exact match/EM (where applicable), BLEU/ROUGE for structured outputs, hallucination-rate (measured by annotator checklist + classifier), safety flags, latency and token-cost variance.
- Regression detection: thresholds are configurable per-account. Default policy: 95% CI drop in primary metric OR >3% absolute increase in hallucination-rate triggers automated triage.

Production monitoring and alerts:
- Real-time telemetry: per-request tokens, latency, top-k logits, safety classifier score, call stack id. Telemetry is sent to our observability pipeline with 90-day default retention; longer retention available under Dedicated/Private plans.
- Traceability: tokens are not stored by default; we store hashed prompt fingerprints and KV cache metadata to enable reconstruction when customers opt-in.
- Incident playbook: automated rollbacks to the last known-good model, immediate canary isolation, and post-mortem with customer-facing summary.

EU AI Act specifics (summary):
- High-risk assessment: when BRH uses our models to provide clinical decision suggestions that influence care, we recommend treating the solution as high-risk. Controls we supply: detailed technical documentation (model cards, training data provenance summary), post-market monitoring (continuous evaluation), human oversight guidance, and data governance contracts (data usage, retention, deletion).
- Conformity assistance: we provide templates for risk management files and support evidence generation for conformity assessment bodies.

Attachments included in Drive: sample-eval-report-BRH-slice-202607.pdf (annotated), SOC2_extract_redacted.pdf, and the NIST mapping PDF Rohan attached.

Happy to walk the committee through the sample report tomorrow.

—Monica

Elena / Team —

Attached is the final deliverable set and links we discussed. Summary of the package:

- Redwood_NIST_Mapping_20260811.pdf — mapping table (Identify/Protect/Detect/Respond/Recover) with references to runbooks, monitoring artifacts, and policy owners.
- Redwood_EU_AIAct_Positioning_20260811.docx — short memo on classification guidance, mandatory technical measures we recommend, and contractual options for customers who designate high-risk use.
- sample-eval-report-BRH-slice-202607.pdf — annotated evaluation showing baseline comparisons, statistical tests, and regression triggers.
- SOC2_extract_redacted.pdf — excerpt of our latest SOC 2 Type II report (shared under the NDA link).
- Drive folder (read-only): https://drive.redwoodinternal.com/BRH/RFP-2026/governance-matrix (contains trace logs, sample manifests, and the eval harness README).

Quick answers to Procurement:
1) Data storage: by default, the hosted API does NOT persist raw prompts or PHI. We store hashed prompt fingerprints and aggregated telemetry. Customers can opt-in to store raw request data under Dedicated/Private deployments or explicit contract terms; this is a common pattern for customers who require full traceability.
2) EU AI Act: we can act as a provider and agree to support conformity artifacts. For high-risk scenarios we typically collaborate with the customer for the conformity assessment; Redwood can provide technical documentation, post-market monitoring reports, and signed attestations where needed (and we will work with your legal team to define the contractual scope).
3) SOC 2: yes — excerpt attached. Full report can be shared under NDA.

Next steps: please confirm if you want a live walkthrough of the eval report and the regression playbook (I recommend a joint session with our security/product team to cover the EU AI Act controls). Proposed times: Thu 14:00–15:00 PT or Fri 09:00–10:00 PT.

Best regards,
